A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SWIRL study. Text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison. The removed trajectory appendix and renumbered model-free appendix can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original SWIRL experiments on simulated gridworld trajectories and two mouse-behavior datasets, together with sensitivity, robustness, and model-free results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments on all three datasets, including inferred rewards, held-out likelihoods, segmentation results, and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: The history-dependent reward/policy model, state-conditioned mode transitions, and EM inference procedure are unchanged. The IQ-Learn extension moves from Appendix D.1 to C.1 without a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 5-by-5 gridworld, water-restricted mouse labyrinth, and spontaneous mouse-behavior datasets. The perturbation scenarios are retained; removing a detailed visualization does not remove task coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MaxEnt and I-1/I-2/S-1/S-2 remain in the gridworld and labyrinth comparisons, with ARHMM and rARHMM additionally evaluated on spontaneous behavior. I-1 and S-1 retain their correspondence to multi-intention IQL and locally consistent IRL.

E3.justification: Reported train/test splits, trajectory lengths, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, and hidden-mode/history-length sweeps are unchanged. The revised labyrinth plots are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix C.1/Figure 8B provides a spatial inspection of an example trajectory supporting home segments ending at nodes 1 or 2; this evidence is removed, although the qualification remains in Section 4.2.2. The sensitivity sweeps and permutation robustness analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten runs, use standard-deviation bands, and specify the same boxplot outlier rule in Appendix B.8. Changed plotted spreads are result changes, without a stated change in uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 3, 5, and 6 revise labyrinth likelihood distributions and reward maps. For example, Figure 6A's S-2 median likelihood shifts approximately from -0.74 to -0.72; Figure 3C changes water-mode leaving/staying rewards from 0.9/0.7 to 0.4/1.0 and adds explore-mode values. Principal rankings and the other datasets' results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The HM-MDP definitions, EM objective and derivations, forward-backward equations, ARHMM connections, and model-free IQ-Learn formulation are retained without substantive mathematical changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: history-dependent switching IRL, interpretable animal-behavior rewards and segmentation, and connections to dynamics-based models. The scope of the central claims is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2.1 shifts the explanation of the post-visit leaving preference from the water-mode reward to explore-mode history dependence. Exploration no longer explicitly excludes the water port, and Section 4.2.2 changes water visits occurring 'at the end' of segments to 'near the end.'

D1.justification: The code-access information and Appendix B implementation details, optimizers, hyperparameters, hardware, runtimes, and metric-computation instructions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, baseline positioning, and novelty claims are unchanged. Adding 'about' to the description of earlier studies' 20-time-point trajectories is a wording refinement.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the labyrinth explanation and small wording changes. The short trajectory appendix is removed, and the model-free appendix and cross-references are renumbered; the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3C expands into separate water/explore diagrams, and labyrinth panels receive changes to axes, boxplot styling, and reward-map displays. v2 Figure 8 is removed, while model-free Figure 9 becomes Figure 8. The example segmentation strips in Figures 3E, 5B, and 6B remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The expanded Figure 3C makes the mode-specific rewards more explicit, and the segment-boundary wording becomes more cautious. However, the PDFs do not establish whether the revised labyrinth results correct earlier errors, and v3 removes detailed spatial support for a retained home-segment interpretation. These changes do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
